sources.title: The Soul of a New Machine
sources.what_it_covers: Pulitzer-winning narrative account of Data General's Eclipse MV/8000 minicomputer project, including intense schedule pressure, hardware debugging crises, and recovery under deadline; predates modern ASIC PD but is the canonical 'design-closure war story' precedent in hardware engineering literature.
sources.why_relevant: Widely cited archetype for hardware design-team crisis/recovery narratives; not physical-design-specific (no congestion/CTS/power-grid detail) but frequently referenced in this genre.
sources.verification_hint: Tracy Kidder "The Soul of a New Machine" Data General Eclipse MV/8000

sources.title: Clock Domain Crossing (CDC) Design & Verification Techniques Using SystemVerilog
sources.what_it_covers: Practical catalog of real CDC failure modes (metastability, reconvergence, gray-coding mistakes) and recovery techniques drawn from field experience, by Clifford E. Cummings.
sources.why_relevant: Detailed, engineer-authored failure/recovery case material directly touching timing-closure-adjacent CDC bugs; SNUG papers are freely posted and widely cited in industry.
sources.verification_hint: site:sunburst-design.com Cummings SNUG clock domain crossing paper

sources.title: Silicon bring-up debugging posts (bunnie:studios blog)
sources.what_it_covers: Andrew 'bunnie' Huang's first-person accounts of chip/board bring-up failures and root-cause debugging on projects like Chumby and Novena, including power and signal-integrity issues discovered post-tapeout.
sources.why_relevant: Rare public, nameable engineer blog with concrete silicon-bring-up failure/recovery narratives, though I cannot recall a single specific post title with confidence.

sources.title: IBM POWER6 circuit and physical design special issue
sources.venue_or_publication: IBM Journal of Research and Development, vol. 51, no. 6
sources.what_it_covers: Follow-on special issue to the POWER4 papers we already hold, covering POWER6 circuit design, timing closure, and physical implementation challenges at a later technology node.
sources.why_relevant: Same rigorous IBM J R&D lineage as the owned POWER4 papers but a distinct chip/generation, likely containing comparable design-closure detail; I am not fully certain of exact article titles/authors within the issue.
sources.verification_hint: "IBM Journal of Research and Development" POWER6 2007 volume 51 issue 6 physical design
